major_features: Custom SQL lexer and AST parser supporting projection, filtering, and aggregate JOIN queries
Columnar binary file writer with run-length encoding (RLE) and dictionary compression schemes
Cost-Based Optimizer (CBO) translating ASTs to physical execution plans using catalog histograms
Physical execution engine implementing the Volcano Iterator model (open/next/close) over column chunks
Hybrid Hash Join and Sort-Merge Join algorithms operating directly on memory-mapped column buffers
Vectorized execution operator processing blocks of values to minimize virtual method call overhead
Dynamic transactional schema evolution engine supporting column addition, deletion, and renaming
Parallel column scan orchestrator utilizing Java 21 Virtual Threads for concurrent block retrieval
candidate_ideas.name: ColumnaDB
candidate_ideas.pain: Slow analytical reports, high memory overhead, and lack of fine-grained column serialization/compression options in standard embedded engines.
candidate_ideas.problem: Row-oriented databases struggle with analytical aggregation queries (OLAP) because they must load entire rows into memory, wasting massive I/O bandwidth on unused columns.
candidate_ideas.solution: A zero-dependency columnar database engine written in Java 21. It implements custom binary storage structures, Run-Length Encoding (RLE), dictionary compression, a Cost-Based Optimizer (CBO) utilizing table statistics, and a Volcano-style vectorized execution model.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Database engineers and systems architects building high-performance analytical query engines.
candidate_ideas.verification: A deterministic test suite that generates synthetic multi-column tables, corrupts specific columnar blocks to test CRC32 integrity, executes nested queries, and asserts that the Cost-Based Optimizer selects the mathematically optimal physical join plan.

major_features: Linux TUN/TAP virtual network interface driver for raw Ethernet frame reading and writing
ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) cache with automatic entry timeout, lookup, and request queueing
IPv4 packet parser and reassembler with TTL handling, options parsing, and header checksum validation
Complete RFC-compliant TCP state machine managing transitions (SYN, ESTABLISHED, FIN-WAIT, etc.)
Sliding window flow control adjusting dynamically based on receiver buffer advertisements
TCP Congestion Control engine implementing Slow Start, Congestion Avoidance, and Fast Retransmit (Tahoe/Reno)
Out-of-order packet reassembly queue utilizing a red-black tree for efficient sequence insertion
Virtual routing table supporting static routes, longest-prefix matching, and gateway redirects
candidate_ideas.name: NetStackC
candidate_ideas.pain: Kernel panic risks when debugging network drivers, high overhead of virtualization, and inability to isolate packet loss scenarios deterministically.
candidate_ideas.problem: Operating system network stacks are monolithic, hard to debug, and run in kernel space, making custom protocol prototyping and deterministic packet-level testing highly complex.
candidate_ideas.solution: A fully-featured userspace TCP/IP stack implemented in C11. It interfaces with a Linux TUN/TAP device to read/write raw Ethernet frames, parsing and managing ARP, IPv4, and a complete TCP state machine with custom sliding-window flow control and congestion management.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Embedded systems developers and network security researchers studying low-level network protocol design.
candidate_ideas.verification: A deterministic packet injection harness that simulates random packet drops, byte duplication, out-of-order delivery, and corrupted checksums, verifying that the sliding window and congestion control engines converge to error-free state delivery.

major_features: Virtual-thread-backed Actor model runtime with non-blocking mailboxes and message-passing
Raft Consensus Protocol engine (Leader Election, Log Replication, Safety, and Joint Consensus membership changes)
Replicated Finite State Machine (FSM) engine with automated snapshotting and log compaction
Deterministic local network simulator simulating packet loss, asymmetric latency, and out-of-order delivery
Append-only binary log storage engine with CRC32 verification and crash-recovery logic
Dynamic cluster membership transition manager supporting single-server changes without service interruption
Jepsen-style chaos harness injecting split-brain partitions, leader crashes, and network partitions
Linearizable read-query engine utilizing lease reads to bypass log replication on read-only transactions
candidate_ideas.name: RaftActor
candidate_ideas.pain: Hard-to-reproduce split-brain scenarios, silent data corruption during leader transitions, and heavy thread-context switching overhead under high concurrent loads.
candidate_ideas.problem: Distributed consensus engines like ZooKeeper or Consul are complex to deploy, while standard Raft libraries hide state transitions, making it hard to inject deterministic partition faults for testing.
candidate_ideas.solution: A lightweight, local-first distributed consensus and actor runtime written in Java 21. It uses Virtual Threads to run hundreds of independent actors communicating via lock-free mailboxes, coordinating a replicated state machine via an in-memory implementation of the Raft consensus protocol.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Distributed systems engineers requiring a highly testable, fault-tolerant consensus layer without heavy external infrastructure.
candidate_ideas.verification: A Jepsen-style fault injection harness that simulates asymmetric network partitions, clock drift, and node crashes over local loopback interfaces, asserting that the cluster consistently maintains linearizability.

major_features: Custom matrix and tensor operations library implemented in pure Python (no NumPy) with backpropagation
Deep Q-Network (DQN) engine with experience replay buffer and target network synchronization
Multi-core CPU and memory allocator simulator generating dynamic, realistic scheduling workloads
Strict Sandboxed Action Interpreter validating agent decisions against hard safety boundaries (e.g., thermal limits)
Feedback loop adapter converting system throughput, latency, and cache-miss metrics into scalar rewards
Normalized state-space encoder transforming raw hardware metrics into optimized neural network input tensors
Deterministic offline replay system for replaying historical workload traces to evaluate policy drift
Policy serialization and rollback module reverting weights if real-time performance drops below a baseline threshold
candidate_ideas.name: NeuroSched
candidate_ideas.pain: High latency spikes in multi-tenant environments, manual parameter tuning cycles, and lack of safe, isolated runtime adaptation mechanisms.
candidate_ideas.problem: Static heuristic schedulers (like round-robin or priority queues) fail to adapt to dynamic, heterogeneous system workloads, leading to CPU starvation or resource underutilization.
candidate_ideas.solution: A safe, zero-dependency local reinforcement learning agent for resource scheduling implemented in Python 3.12. It features a custom tensor-math and neural-network library written from scratch, training an agent via Q-learning to optimize CPU/Memory task allocations in a simulated multi-core system.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Systems software engineers and researchers designing self-optimizing runtimes and operating system schedulers.
candidate_ideas.verification: An offline training simulator that runs deterministic workloads, asserts that the agent never executes illegal/unsafe states, and verifies that the policy converges to a scheduling efficiency within 5% of a mathematical optimum.

major_features: Custom SHA-1 content-addressable storage engine mapping files to hashed directory paths
Binary object serializer implementing a lightweight LZW compression codec for blob storage
Index (staging area) parser and writer supporting state tracking, file metadata, and conflict markers
Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) commit traverser detecting ancestor relationships and finding common merge bases
Myers' O(ND) difference algorithm producing line-level patches between arbitrary file versions
Three-way merge engine (diff3 equivalent) resolving non-overlapping edits and flagging overlapping conflicts
Packfile generator compiling multiple loose blobs into unified delta-compressed archives with binary indexes
Transactional ref-manager ensuring branch, tag, and HEAD updates are atomic and resilient to crashes
candidate_ideas.name: GitLite
candidate_ideas.pain: High resource overhead of executing external processes, difficulty in programmatically managing merge conflicts, and opaque binary packfile structures.
candidate_ideas.problem: Standard Git is a complex, heavy binary with an extensive C footprint, making it difficult to embed in custom environments, run deterministically in memory, or audit for security compliance.
candidate_ideas.solution: A complete, low-level, Git-compatible content-addressable version control system written in C11. It implements a custom SHA-1 filesystem store, delta-compression packing, Myers' O(ND) diffing, and a three-way merge engine.
candidate_ideas.target_user: Systems programmers, DevOps engineers, and tool builders who want to embed lightweight, custom version control workflows directly into their applications.
candidate_ideas.verification: A deterministic test harness creating highly complex branching topologies, executing concurrent merges, injecting corrupted/truncated object files, and asserting that the diff/merge engine resolves conflicts identically to canonical Git.

known_limitations: Gemini discovery reasons from model knowledge; the factory does not claim live market research or verified market demand.

A passing systems release proves the generated source compiled or byte-compiled and its factory-required unit/integration suites passed; it does not by itself prove production-scale reliability, security certification, or benchmark superiority.
Generated systems projects intentionally use standard-library-only Java 21, C11, or Python 3.12 profiles so validation can be deterministic and does not depend on unverifiable third-party packages.

Hard projects are scoped implementations of real mechanisms, not claims of complete compatibility with Redis, full SQL standards, industrial compilers, or frontier machine-learning systems unless the tests and documentation explicitly demonstrate that scope.
